pageCache.pageTitle: Why the Pre-School Year Matters More Than Ever - Latest News - Micklefield School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Why the Pre-School Year Matters More Than Ever
Parents often ask what children really need before starting school. Is it reading? Writing their name? Counting to 20?
In reality, the research around school readiness tells us something far more important: the strongest predictor of a happy and successful start to school is not academic ability alone, but confidence, communication skills, emotional resilience and curiosity. That is why the pre-school year has become such a vital stage in a child’s development.
Early childhood experts increasingly refer to the years between three and five as a “golden window” for learning. During this period, children’s brains are developing at an extraordinary rate, building the foundations not just for academic achievement, but for social skills, emotional wellbeing and lifelong attitudes towards learning. Crucially, children learn these skills best through play, relationships and real-world experiences, not through pressure or formal schooling too soon. A high-quality pre-school environment bridges the gap beautifully between nursery and Reception. It gently introduces structure and independence while protecting the joy, creativity and imagination that young children need in order to thrive.
At Micklefield School in Reigate, the Pre-Reception year is designed around exactly this philosophy. Rather than focusing narrowly on early academics, the school’s bespoke School Ready Programme nurtures the characteristics that research consistently links to future success: resilience, communication, problem-solving, independence and a love of learning. Children are encouraged to explore, ask questions, collaborate and think creatively. They take part in specialist lessons including music, PE, French and cookery, enjoy outdoor learning and community enrichment activities, and become familiar with the routines and rhythms of school life, all within a nurturing early years environment.
This matters because starting school is about far more than sitting at a table or recognising letters. Teachers consistently say that children who settle most successfully into Reception are those who can manage transitions confidently, communicate their needs, form positive relationships and approach new experiences with curiosity and confidence.
The best pre-school programmes also recognise the importance of emotional security. Strong relationships with trusted adults help children feel safe enough to take risks, build friendships and develop independence. Micklefield’s key person approach ensures every child is known as an individual and supported accordingly.
There is also growing awareness that modern childhood can feel increasingly hurried. Many parents are now actively seeking environments that allow children to develop at the right pace, where wellbeing, outdoor play and creativity are valued alongside academic preparation. In this sense, the pre-school year is no longer simply a waiting room before “real school” begins. It is a hugely important stage in its own right.
Done well, it gives children something invaluable: the confidence to walk into Reception feeling secure, capable and excited to learn. And that may be the very best start of all.
Visit out Nursery pages to find out more!
Want to arrange a visit? or have any queries you would like to discuss? please contact our Admissions Registrar, Kirsty Vines who would love to help!

Year 2 Spread Kindness with Wellbeing Activity
Year 2 came together for a wonderful wellbeing activity this week, focused on kindness and friendship.
Each child had a balloon shape attached to their back, and their classmates took turns writing kind messages on one another’s balloons. By the end of the activity, every child had received thoughtful comments from their peers, making it a truly special experience.
It was a joy to read the uplifting messages, including “You are kind,” “You make me smile,” and “You are a good Red Cap.” The activity brightened everyone’s day and reminded us all of the importance of kindness and encouragement within our school community.

RGS + RGSSH A Level Results
Last Thursday was A Level Results Day and I am delighted to share with you the exceptional achievements of students at both senior schools in the RGS family.
At Reigate Grammar School, the Class of 2026 achieved one of the strongest sets of results in the school's history, with a record 38% of all A Level grades awarded A*, 76% at A*–A and 94% at A*–B. Twenty-four students achieved A*s in every A Level subject they studied, and every student holding an Oxford or Cambridge offer secured their place. Students are now heading to leading universities including Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial, UCL and Durham, while others are taking up sports scholarships in the United States or highly competitive degree apprenticeships in engineering and technology, accounting, banking and finance.
At RGS Surrey Hills, there was much to celebrate, with a significant rise in top grades and the proportion of A*–A grades more than doubling this year, alongside some exceptional individual achievements. Every student applying to university secured a place at their first-choice institution, with destinations including King's College London, Durham, UCL, Exeter and the Royal Veterinary College, as well as international destinations in Boston, Barcelona and Gothenburg. These results reflect the growing academic momentum at RGS Surrey Hills, with rising expectations, investment in excellent teaching and a strengthening curriculum.
Across both schools, these achievements reflect something that matters greatly to the RGS family: enabling every young person to fulfil their potential and leave school ready to pursue their own ambitions. For our younger pupils, these results are an exciting reminder of just how far their own educational journey can take them.
I am sure you will join me in congratulating the RGS and RGSSH Classes of 2026 on all they have achieved.

pageCache.text:
RGS + RGSSH GCSE Results
Last week brought another round of exciting news from across the Reigate Grammar School family. Following on from the recent A Level successes, GCSE Results Day on Thursday 20th August, saw more outstanding achievements by students at both Reigate Grammar School and RGS Surrey Hills.
At Reigate Grammar School, the Class of 2026 achieved the strongest GCSE results in the school’s history. Nearly half of all grades awarded were Grade 9, almost three quarters were at Grades 9–8 and 90% at Grades 9–7, with exceptional results spanning mathematics and science, languages, humanities and the creative arts.
At RGS Surrey Hills, the results tell a compelling story of progress, with three quarters of pupils exceeding their baseline predictions and some achieving, on average, two grades higher than expected. Overall, 80% of GCSE grades were awarded at Grades 9–5, while creative subjects achieved 100% Grades 9–4 and mathematics recorded its strongest results for the third consecutive year.
Behind these results lies a great deal of hard work and commitment from the students, together with the support of their teachers and families. It is a pleasure to share their achievements with you and to congratulate them on all that they have accomplished.
Attached below are the individual GCSE results press releases from both senior schools where you can read more about this year’s achievements.

Big Beginnings Start at Micklefield!
Give your child a happy, nurturing start at Micklefield Nursery. Welcoming children from age 2, we combine the warmth and care of a much-loved nursery with the opportunities and expertise of Micklefield School.
Open year-round | 15 & 30 funded hours available | Just minutes from Reigate station
A happy start. An excellent preparation.
At Micklefield, children are known, nurtured and encouraged to flourish. Through play, exploration and carefully planned learning, our experienced Early Years team helps each child build confidence, independence and a genuine love of learning. As part of Micklefield School, nursery children also benefit from the richness of school life and specialist experiences, while enjoying the security and warmth of their own age-appropriate environment.
“My son runs into nursery every morning with a smile — the staff are amazing and he’s grown so much in confidence.” – Nursery Parent
Why families choose Micklefield Nursery
From age 2

Mr Mark Elsey
Mark joined the Board of Governors of Reigate Grammar School in 2012 and has been Chair since December 2021.
Educated at Reigate Grammar School and King’s College London, Mr Elsey attended Chancery Lane Law School before joining Cameron Markby as a trainee solicitor. He is now a Partner at Ashurst where he heads up the Energy, Transport and Infrastructure sector.
Mark's son and daughter both attended Reigate Grammar School. His family connections with the school are extensive: he met his wife, Jacqueline,â€¯while at RGS; his father and father-in-law both attended the school. Mark is a member of Old Reigatian RFC and of Reigate Heath Golf Club. His charity work includes his role as Board member atâ€¯Great Ormond Street Hospital Raising the Roof Charity and Chairman of the RGS London Professional Group, in support of the RGS Foundation raising funds towards ‘needs blind’ entry to RGS.
Mr Duncan Anderson
Duncan was a Micklefield Governor from 2018 and joined the RGS Board in 2024 when the schools merged. He is a member of the Finance & Foundation Committee.
Duncan was educated at Hereford Cathedral School before graduating in mathematics from Cambridge University and then qualifying as a Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries.
He has worked for WTW and its predecessor companies (Watsons, Watson Wyatt, EMB, Towers Watson) for over 35 years, in both general insurance consultancy and related software development.â€¯ He specialises in motor insurance pricing analytics and has spoken on this in seminars in over 30 countries.â€¯ Since 2017 he has led WTW’s global Insurance Technology business, which provides specialist software to over 1,000 insurers worldwide.
Duncan is married with four daughters, all of whom attended RGS.â€¯ He has been a resident of Reigate since 1990.
Dr Shrilla Banerjee
Shrilla joined the Board of Governors in 2021 and is a member of the Education & Welfare Committee.
Shrilla is a Consultant Cardiologist with a specialist interest in prevention and intervention (angioplasty and stenting) of coronary artery disease. Her research interests lie in Women’s Cardiovascular Health and she wasâ€¯also a Cardiologist for the Civil Aviation Authority assessing fitness to fly of commercial and private pilot licence holders.
In her current position at East Surrey Hospital, Dr Banerjee is the Lead forâ€¯Education, responsible for the training and supervision of cardiology trainees, and runs the cardiology Education programme. â€¯She is also an NHS Ambassador for Education, involved in the work experience programme for schools.
She was elected on to the Council of the British Cardiovascular Society and the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society, where she Chaired the Focus Group for Women in Interventional Cardiologyâ€¯looking at how we can attract more women into Interventional Cardiology, support existing female trainees and Consultants and ensure excellent representation and visibility of women in the field.
Outside of work, Shrilla enjoys spending time with her family, keeping fit and painting.
Mr Marc Benton
Marc is the Chair of the Finance & Foundation Committee and has been Governor on the RGS Board since 2015.
Marc has worked for the North Sea Transition Authority (the “NSTA”) since 2020 as the Head of Investor Finance. The NSTA is part of the UK Government charged with regulating the UK offshore oil and gas industry and developing the energy transition. Prior to this role, Marc was an experienced Managing Director with a successful 23 year history of working in the investment banking industry.â€¯ Skilled in M&A and general corporate advisory, Capital Markets funding (equity and debt/high yield) and general Corporate Finance for Corporates, NOCs and Private Equity.â€¯ He led regional investment banking sector teams for 12 years in both EMEA and APAC. He has a Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) with French from the University of Birmingham and a European Master of Business Science from Ecole Superieure de Commerce, Clermont Ferrand, France.
Helen Crossley
A former St. Christopher’s Governor, Helen joined the RGS Board of Governors following the merger with St Christopher’s in May 2025. She sits on the Education and Welfare Committee.
Helen became a governor of St Christopher’s in 2012 following her retirement as Head of the Prep School at Ewell Castle. Having previously held the post of Deputy Head of the Junior school at City of London Freemen’s School. She was Chair of Governor’s at St Christopher’s from November 2016 to June 2021.
Helen is delighted to be able to use the experience she has gained throughout her career in a strategic role within the RGS group of schools with a particular focus on the Prep and Pre-Prep age groups.
Mr Chris Dixon
A former Chinthurst Governor, Chris joined the RGS Board of Governors in March 2017 and is a member of the Estates and Premises Committee.
Chris was educated at Malvern College, Worcestershire. Chris then went on to study a combined honours degree in Economics and Geography at Exeter University, following which he joined the University’s Law School, where he achieved a Diploma in Law and sat his LPC.
Chris is a solicitor with a specialism in commercial and residential property. â€¯Over a 14 years period, Chris climbed up the ranks at Ashurst in London. â€¯He then moved for 7 years toâ€¯Rawlinson Butler in Crawley. He is now a partner at Bowles & Co in Epsom.
Chris is married with two children, both formerly at Chinthurst, then going to Epsom College.
Mrs Mary Edmunds
Mary joined the Board of Governors of Reigate Grammar School in 2018 with a focus on strategy, people and growth.
Mary sits on the board for Hines Europe Limited, a global commercial real estate firm. Educated in the US with global experience in business transformation, human resources and strategy, Mrs Edmunds arrived at Reigate Grammar School with a global perspective. Mrs Edmunds is a Senior Managing Director for Hines Real Estate. She studied Economics and Psychology at Vanderbilt University in the United States and her Masters of Business at Exeter University, UK.
Mrs. Edmunds has worked in business education with Harvard University since 2014 to deliver leadership programmes for a sovereign wealth fund in the Middle East. Having seen education from a global perspective and taking a deep interest in the future of Reigate Grammar School,
Mary is married with two daughters, who both have graduated from Reigate Grammar School.
Mrs Joosje Hamilton
Joosje was appointed a governor at RGS in June 2024 following the merger with Micklefield – before that she was Chair of Governors at Micklefield School since December 2017. Joosje is a member of the Education & Welfare Committee.
She is a solicitor specialising in EU and UK competition and regulatory law and sits on the Education & Staffing Committee. â€¯A few years ago, she decided to leave full-time employment in the City and became a part-time legal consultant.â€¯ She now spends the majority of her time running and developing her family’s agricultural estate, including managing its residential and commercial property portfolio. â€¯Joosje’s three daughters had a wonderful education and happy time at Micklefield School and RGS and she is therefore delighted to contribute to the future success of the RGS Group of Schools.
Mrs Maxine Hulme
Maxine is Vice Chair of the RGS Board and Chair of the Governance and Risk Committee. She joined the RGS Board following the partnership between RGS and Chinthurst School, announced in March 2017. She was previously the Chair of Governors at Chinthurst School.
Maxine has been working in the private sector since 2016 within financial services where she has worked in financial services transformation and is currently an operations Director.
In her earlier career, Maxine served as Deputy Assistant Commissioner in the Metropolitan Police Service, holding senior roles in Transformation, Operations and Intelligence. In recognition of outstanding service, she was awarded the Queen’s Policing Medal in 2014.
Mrs Lisa Page
Lisa joined the RGS board after the partnership between RGS and Chinthurst was announced in March 2017. She was appointed Chair of Education and Welfare for the RGS group in March 2025.â€¯
She is an accomplished Healthcare Director with a career in operational management within the UK's Healthcare sector with a strong track record in growing private patient healthcare services within NHS trusts,â€¯ within some of the world's leading hospitals in London.â€¯â€¯
Throughout her career Lisa has held a range of senior leadership roles with operational oversight, strategic planning and complex capital projects across multiple sites. She is passionate about service excellence and consistently delivering outstanding outcomes, which has been recognised through multiple awards for best hospital performance.â€¯
Lisa has extensive international travel experience to expand services abroad whilst establishing and strengthening strategic global partnerships.
Mr Dominic Roberts
Dominic joined the RGS Board of Governors in May 2025 following the merger with St Christopher’s and is on the Finance and Foundation committee. He was previously the Chair at St Christopher’s School.
After studying Physics at Bristol University Dominic became a Chartered Accountant and, upon becoming a partner in 2005, specialising in providing advice to Companies looking to IPO or already listed on the London stock markets. Since 2019 he has been the managing partner of PKF in London, Leeds and Manchester, responsible for setting and overseeing the strategic and operational direction of the business and its people. He is also Chair of the EMEI region of the PKF Global Accounting Network and a Global Board member.
Dominic is the father of two girls who attended St Christopher’s and continue to cherish the friends and memories from their years at the school many years later.
Mrs Maggie Stilwell
Maggie joined the Board in 2023 and is a member of the Finance & Foundation Committee.
Maggie has recently retired as a Partner at EY, having worked for the firm for 28 years specialising in forensic accountancy. Maggie has worked across industries for clients during that time, as well as having a senior management position for the firm of EY. Maggie has given evidence to courts and arbitrations on behalf of her clients, and acted as judge for commercial disputes requiring an expert determination process. Prior to working at EY, Maggie worked at PwC in the audit practice, qualifying as a Chartered Accountant. She holds a First Class Honours degree in Business from Edinburgh University.

Rebecca joined the board following the merger with Micklefield in 2024 and is a member of the Education & Welfare Committee.
Rebecca graduated from Cambridge University with a master’s in manufacturing engineering. She worked in the energy sector and medical equipment manufacturing before becoming a teacher in 2004. She has worked in education for 20 years as a maths teacher and more recently has also been an EPQ coordinator.
Mr Chris Townsend
Chris was a Governor on the Board at Boxhill School previously and joined the RGS Board following the merger in 2025. Chris is a member of the Education & Welfare committee and oversees the Boarding at RGS Surrey Hills.
Chris has been the Head at Felsted School in Essex for the last decade, having previously worked at Stowe and Dean Close. He taught Classics and has also held roles as Deputy Head, Head of Boarding and Master in charge of Cricket and was a Housemaster of both day and boarding houses. In April 2026, he will take up the Headship at Cheltenham College.â€¯ Chris is also on the Board at Essex Cricket club and is a trustee of the charity Chance to Shine, as well as being an ISI Inspector.
Mr Nick Weber
Nick joined the Board of Governors of Reigate Grammar School in 2018 and is a member of the Finance & Foundation Committee.
He holds a degree in Chemical Engineering from Princeton University. All five of his children have been educated at Reigate Grammar School.
Nick is the Founder and CEO of Henderson Park, a 92 person real estate investment firm focused on the UK and Continental Europe. Henderson Park manages $6 billion of investor equity, and to date has invested over $14 billion in building a portfolio of real estate assets across Europe.
Prior to founding Henderson Park, Nick was a founding partner at Mount Kellett, an $8 billion multi-asset class investment platform, and ran its European operations from 2008 to 2015. Before joining Mount Kellett, Nick spent 15 years at Goldman Sachs, becoming a partner in 2006.
Mr Ed Wheeler
Ed is the Chair of the Estates & Premises Committee and joined the RGS Board in 2021.
Educated at Douai School, Reading and the Polytechnic of the South Bank, Ed qualified as a Chartered Quantity Surveyor in 1986, becoming a Fellow of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors in 1994. He joined his firm as a Director in 1987 and has been Chairman since 1997.
His practice encompasses all aspects of construction cost and contract consultancy and has successfully delivered a wide range of commissions for major national and international Clients as well as UK developers, public authorities, charities and private clients often working closely with world renowned design teams.
Ed is a member of Old Reigatian RFC and the MCC and is married with two sons, both of whom attended RSM and RGS.

Why Role Play Still Matters
Why Role Play Still Matters: A Modern Perspective on Early Years Development
In a world increasingly shaped by screens and structured routines, the simple act of children “pretending” can sometimes be underestimated. Yet role play remains one of the most powerful and developmentally rich experiences in early childhood, forming a vital foundation for communication, creativity and emotional wellbeing.
Research consistently highlights the importance of play-based learning, with role play at its heart. From an early age, children experiment with symbolic play, using objects to represent something else or imitating everyday experiences. As they grow, this develops into more complex, collaborative scenarios where they create narratives, assign roles and negotiate shared imaginary worlds. These experiences are not just playful—they are essential building blocks for higher-order thinking.
One of the most significant benefits of role play is its impact on language development. In imaginative scenarios, children naturally extend their vocabulary, practise sentence structures and gain confidence in expressing themselves. They also learn the rhythm of conversation—listening, responding and adapting their language to different situations. At a time when speech and language delays are increasingly noted, this kind of meaningful interaction is invaluable.
Role play also plays a crucial role in supporting social and emotional development. As children negotiate roles and explore different perspectives, they learn to take turns, solve problems and understand the feelings of others. This helps to build empathy and resilience. It also provides a safe space to process real-life experiences, allowing children to make sense of the world around them.
Well-designed environments and sensitive adult support can further enrich these experiences. Open-ended resources and themed play areas can spark ideas, while adults can gently extend learning through thoughtful questions or new vocabulary without interrupting the flow of play. However, the most important element is giving children the freedom to lead.
Ultimately, role play may appear simple, but its impact is profound. It nurtures the curiosity, confidence and creativity children need—not only for school, but for life.

pageCache.text:
Allergy Awareness Assembly with Miss Rule
This week, Miss Rule led a whole school assembly focusing on ‘Anaphylaxis’ and the importance of being ‘Allergy Aware’. The children learned what an allergic reaction is and discovered that around 8 in 100 children have an anaphylactic allergy. A key message was that you cannot always see an allergy, making awareness and understanding even more important.
As part of the learning, the school has welcomed a special visitor – an allergy awareness doll called Ruby. Ruby has anaphylaxis to milk and sesame and also has hay fever and asthma. Throughout the week, Ruby will be visiting classes and helping to bring learning to life through practical medical allergy scenarios.
During the assembly, the children were introduced to the 14 main allergens and discussed ways they can help keep everyone safe. They shared thoughtful ideas, including not sharing snacks, looking out for friends with allergies and knowing how to get help quickly if someone is having a reaction.
This important initiative is helping to build understanding, empathy and responsibility across the school community, ensuring that everyone plays a part in keeping each other safe.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why the Pre-School Year Matters More Than Ever - Latest News - Micklefield School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Why the Pre-School Year Matters More Than Ever
Parents often ask what children really need before starting school. Is it reading? Writing their name? Counting to 20?
In reality, the research around school readiness tells us something far more important: the strongest predictor of a happy and successful start to school is not academic ability alone, but confidence, communication skills, emotional resilience and curiosity. That is why the pre-school year has become such a vital stage in a child’s development.
Early childhood experts increasingly refer to the years between three and five as a “golden window” for learning. During this period, children’s brains are developing at an extraordinary rate, building the foundations not just for academic achievement, but for social skills, emotional wellbeing and lifelong attitudes towards learning. Crucially, children learn these skills best through play, relationships and real-world experiences, not through pressure or formal schooling too soon. A high-quality pre-school environment bridges the gap beautifully between nursery and Reception. It gently introduces structure and independence while protecting the joy, creativity and imagination that young children need in order to thrive.
At Micklefield School in Reigate, the Pre-Reception year is designed around exactly this philosophy. Rather than focusing narrowly on early academics, the school’s bespoke School Ready Programme nurtures the characteristics that research consistently links to future success: resilience, communication, problem-solving, independence and a love of learning. Children are encouraged to explore, ask questions, collaborate and think creatively. They take part in specialist lessons including music, PE, French and cookery, enjoy outdoor learning and community enrichment activities, and become familiar with the routines and rhythms of school life, all within a nurturing early years environment.
This matters because starting school is about far more than sitting at a table or recognising letters. Teachers consistently say that children who settle most successfully into Reception are those who can manage transitions confidently, communicate their needs, form positive relationships and approach new experiences with curiosity and confidence.
The best pre-school programmes also recognise the importance of emotional security. Strong relationships with trusted adults help children feel safe enough to take risks, build friendships and develop independence. Micklefield’s key person approach ensures every child is known as an individual and supported accordingly.
There is also growing awareness that modern childhood can feel increasingly hurried. Many parents are now actively seeking environments that allow children to develop at the right pace, where wellbeing, outdoor play and creativity are valued alongside academic preparation. In this sense, the pre-school year is no longer simply a waiting room before “real school” begins. It is a hugely important stage in its own right.
Done well, it gives children something invaluable: the confidence to walk into Reception feeling secure, capable and excited to learn. And that may be the very best start of all.

Celebrating Former Pupil Success: The Reigate Soap Company
We are delighted to celebrate the inspiring achievements of former pupil Leon, whose entrepreneurial venture, The Reigate Soap Company, is already making a meaningful impact. Some of you may have recently met Leon and his co-founder Toby at Micklefest, where their innovative business captured plenty of attention.
Together, Leon and Toby have created an eco-friendly solution to everyday handwashing, delivering refillable hand soap by bicycle. Their approach not only reduces waste but also helps cut carbon emissions – a fantastic example of young people taking action for a more sustainable future. Through their partnership with CleanHub, every bottle sold also contributes to removing 1kg of plastic before it reaches the ocean, further amplifying their positive environmental impact.
From building their own website using AI tools to achieving an impressive 100% conversion rate on some door-to-door sales days, Leon and Toby are demonstrating what can be achieved with passion, creativity and determination.
Reflecting on their journey, the boys shared this advice: “Never give up. It’s hard work, but if we can do it, anyone can.”
We are incredibly proud of Leon and all he has accomplished so far, and we look forward to seeing The Reigate Soap Company continue to grow.
